title: Why we still oil our oak by hand
intro: Lacquer is faster and oil takes days. Here's why every table that leaves our workshop is still finished by hand.

content.text: A sprayed lacquer finish takes about an hour. Our oil finish takes three days. Every few months someone asks whether we have considered switching, and the answer is always the same: we have, and we won’t.

We sand every surface by hand to a fine grit, then work in a thin coat of hardwax oil with a pad. The oil soaks into the wood rather than sitting on top of it. After a day we buff away the excess and repeat, three times in total.

body.caption: An oiled Ferris tabletop, a few weeks into daily life. Photo by Mélyna Côté on Unsplash.

body.note: Every Ferris table gets three coats of hardwax oil and comes with a care kit for the years ahead.

content.text: An oiled table feels like wood, not plastic. It will pick up marks, and that is the point: a scratch can be sanded out and re-oiled at home in ten minutes, while damaged lacquer has to be stripped and sprayed again.
Re-oil once or twice a year, more often if the table sees a lot of use. You will notice the grain deepen and the colour warm with every coat.
